business_quality.justification: An excellent operator: 25.4% operating margin, 19.0% FCF margin, three-year revenue CAGR of 22.3% and net income CAGR of 30.9%, with no base-year distortion. Q2 2026 revenue of $8.76B was up 55% year on year. Deducted for what the margin is built on - connectors and interconnect are a competitive, capital-consuming business, and the current margin reflects extraordinary volume leverage rather than a structural step-change.

competitive_advantage.justification: Real advantages: enormous breadth of catalogue, design-in relationships that make Amphenol hard to displace mid-programme, and manufacturing scale. But interconnect is not a monopoly - Amphenol competes directly with TE Connectivity, Molex and others, and customers deliberately dual-source. The moat is durable but it is a cost-and-scale moat, not a pricing-power moat.

catalysts.justification: Specific, dated and currently favourable: Q3 2026 revenue guided to $9.3-9.4B, implying 50-52% year-on-year growth, which was about 7% above what the market expected. IT datacom is 43% of sales and grew 89% year on year (63% organically), with AI products driving essentially all of the 22% sequential growth. The CommScope acquisition adds further interconnect exposure. These are genuine catalysts, not hopes.

risk_reward.justification: The lowest risk/reward score here, and deliberately so. Every attractive number above is an AI-capex number. With 43% of sales in a segment growing 89%, the trailing multiple of 23.2x is being applied to earnings that embed a boom. My own lessons file warns against buying a cyclical at a full multiple on peak trailing figures - that is precisely this setup. A datacentre capex digestion phase takes that segment from +89% to negative, and the multiple and the earnings compress together. Base +16% against a bear of -38%.

management.justification: A strong long-run record of disciplined acquisitions integrated without destroying returns, which is rare in industrials. Executing well through an extraordinary demand period. Withheld one point because share count rose 4.6% over the window - modest dilution at a time of record profitability, when buybacks would have been the shareholder-friendlier choice.
